summary.headline: Borosil Renewables Q2 FY27 solar glass sales were INR382.1 crore with EBITDA margin down to 30.4% on furnace maintenance and a 2.8% price cut, with October output reported higher.
summary.overview: Standalone H1 FY27 sales rose 12.8% to INR801.8 crore and EBITDA rose 18.5% to INR258.3 crore, but Q2 alone showed softer numbers. Q2 solar glass sales were flat YoY at INR382.1 crore, with EBITDA of INR116.34 crore at 30.4% margin versus 33% a year earlier, because of furnace maintenance (production down about 4.5-5%) and a reduced fuel surcharge after gas prices eased in July. Management said the fuel surcharge was restored in October as gas prices rebounded, and that October production was strong and above prior levels. The 600 tpd expansion (about 60% capacity addition, project cost raised by INR150 crore to about INR1,100 crore) is on track for commissioning toward end-Q4 FY27, funded internally without extra bank debt.

segments.name: Solar glass (core)
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 sales INR382.1 crore at 30.4% EBITDA margin; volume dip from furnace maintenance and a 2.8% price decline from reduced fuel surcharge. Management expects margins to return to higher levels by end of Q2/Q3.

segments.name: Solar kits (trading)
segments.commentary: Revenue of INR14.1 crore in Q2 FY27 (INR15.4 crore in H1) with negligible EBITDA. Sales are being made in batches, with module and inverter purchases of about INR14 crore shown as purchase stocking credit.

segments.name: Rooftop solar (new)
segments.commentary: Early-stage B2C/C&I rooftop business launched in four states with distributors appointed and some projects executed. Management said margins are low as the business is largely trading, and it is not yet profitable at scale.

segments.name: Overseas subsidiaries
segments.commentary: No net revenue in Q2 FY27 and negative EBITDA of INR0.11 crore, versus INR5.08 crore loss in Q2 FY26.

guidance_outlook: Management expects October output to continue at high levels and to make good the Q2 shortfall within FY27; the production dip was about 4.5-5%, with output now said to be 8-10% above earlier levels (early, not yet sustained).
Management expects EBITDA margins of at least 30% going forward and 31-32% in FY27 and FY28 (based on current parameters), with fuel surcharge restored in October.
600 tpd capacity addition (about 60% increase) is expected to be commissioned toward end-Q4 FY27; furnace 1 and furnace 2 firing planned in February and March 2027.
Furnaces SG1 and SG2 may each need a 75-day rebuild, most likely in H1 FY28; management says no production loss is expected in FY27 and expects the new capacity to offset the outage.

Project cost raised by INR150 crore to about INR1,100 crore, funded internally (INR800 crore internal, INR300 crore debt already sanctioned but not drawn); management says no further dilution foreseen.
Company expects to be net cash positive by end-March 2027; a decision on new growth areas is expected by end of FY27.
Expansion of 60% expected to add 2-3% EBITDA margin via operating leverage from the new facility.
capex_capacity: 600 tpd new capacity at existing site, about 60% increase; total project cost about INR1,100 crore after an INR150 crore revision (about 20% from exchange rate, balance from fuel-cost-saving equipment and power redundancy of about INR25 crore).

Capital work-in-progress rose to INR349 crore at September 2026 from INR107 crore at March 2026; LCs of about INR150 crore plus advances outstanding; building nearly complete and machine deliveries under way.
Installation to start by end of Q3 FY27; furnaces to be fired in February and March 2027.
Existing furnaces run at full capacity; SG1 and SG2 (operating about 7 years) to be rebuilt, 75 days each, likely H1 FY28.
Domestic solar glass supply of about 18 GW versus demand of about 62 GW DC; module capacity 233 GW; cell capacity about 38 GW rising to about 75 GW by 2027.
demand_pricing: Average ex-factory realisation INR155.9 per square metre in Q2 FY27, down from INR160.3 in Q1 FY27; the INR4.4 drop was due to the reduced fuel surcharge. Management expects a return to about INR160 by quarter end.

Fuel surcharge was partly rolled back in July after gas prices eased, then raised again in October as Brent and gas prices rose to about USD115 (versus about USD100 when first passed on and USD75-80 at the rollback).

Soda ash (about 30-32% of raw material cost) price up about 10% from June to September quarter; imported dolomite and limestone costs and China freight rates also rose. Management plans to shift dolomite sourcing from 30-40% domestic toward more domestic supply.
Anti-dumping duty on China and Vietnam in place until December 2029; management sees domestic supply shortfall supporting pricing.
Management says there is no cost-plus or pass-through for raw materials; the fuel surcharge was a one-off force majeure recovery, so productivity gains are needed to offset other cost increases.

qa_highlights.question: What was the revenue and EBITDA loss from the Q2 production disruption?
qa_highlights.answer: Management put the revenue loss at about INR15 crore, with production down about 4.5% due to furnace maintenance; output has since recovered and exceeded earlier levels.

qa_highlights.question: Why did raw material costs rise and can margins return to 30%+?
qa_highlights.answer: Soda ash prices rose about 10%, imported dolomite and freight costs increased, and the fuel surcharge was reduced; management expects margins to recover through restored surcharge, higher volumes, and domestic sourcing savings.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 600 tpd expansion fully funded and what is the debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR800 crore is internal funds (from preferential issues already received) and INR300 crore is previously signed debt not yet drawn; no further dilution is foreseen.

qa_highlights.question: How will SG1 and SG2 rebuilds affect FY28 volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 75-day shutdowns are planned for H1 FY28, expected to be offset by the new line; it also said this is speculative and volume recovery cannot be guaranteed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the rooftop solar strategy and margin profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Rooftop is at an early stage in four states, using the Borosil brand and distributors; management said margins will be low as it is largely trading and that scale is needed before profit improves.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue contribution expected from the new capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects turnover to rise about 60% in line with capacity, with 2-3% EBITDA margin gain from operating leverage.

risks_watch: Gas and crude price volatility (Brent cited at about USD115): fuel surcharge pass-through has lagged cost moves in both directions, and management has not yet restored the Q1 realisation level.
Commissioning and ramp-up of the 600 tpd line by end-Q4 FY27; the INR150 crore cost overrun and the power-redundancy and exchange-rate items.
Demand and sell-through of about 1,600 tpd of new capacity; management did not commit to specific customer contracts beyond discussions.
Planned 75-day rebuilds of SG1 and SG2 in H1 FY28, and management's refusal to guarantee recovery of lost volume.
Soda ash, dolomite and freight cost inflation with no contractual pass-through; progress on domestic sourcing shift to be monitored.
Rooftop and solar kit ventures are low margin and small; the management target for their revenue was not quantified.
Overseas subsidiaries are loss-making, though loss narrowed sharply in Q2 FY27.
summary.management_tone: Confident on recovery and demand, with management repeatedly saying October output was strong and the shortfall would be made up. Cautious and evasive on specifics: Chairman called volume make-up "speculative", would not commit to exact margins beyond "at least 30%", and deferred the tax and cash-flow queries to Investor Relations.
key_quotes: Our company is making glass at a higher rate than anywhere else in the world per square meter.
We cannot guarantee that we make up the volume loss.
As a company in corporate philosophy, we do not believe in overstretching ourselves to the point that management suffers.

adds.what: 600 tpd solar glass capacity at existing site (~60% increase, to ~1,600 tpd)

growth.why: Management guides FY28 volume to ~1,600 tpd (60% above current) and EBITDA margins back to 31-32%, backed by the 600 tpd line (INR1,100 crore, furnaces fired Feb-Mar 2027, commissioning toward end-Q4 FY27) and fuel-surcharge restoration, though the 75-day SG1/SG2 rebuild in H1 FY28 and no raw-material pass-through add execution risk.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides margins back to at least 30% and 31-32% in FY27-FY28 with fuel surcharge restored in October and realisation expected back near INR160, plus 2-3% operating leverage from the new line.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 600 tpd line (about 60% addition to ~1,600 tpd) is under construction at INR1,100 crore, with capital WIP at INR349 crore and furnaces to be fired Feb-Mar 2027.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management expects FY28 output of about 1,600 tpd (60% above current) and October output 8-10% above earlier levels, though the Chairman called make-up of the Q2 shortfall speculative.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: The current expansion is already sized and funded (INR800 crore internal, INR300 crore sanctioned debt), and a decision on new growth areas is due by end-FY27, but no new plant is named; the 60% step-up leaves no near-term announced capex.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Q2 solar glass EBITDA margin fell to 30.4% from 33% and realisation dropped to INR155.9/sqm from INR160.3, so management is guiding to recovery, not to a raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Gas and Brent near USD115 with surcharge pass-through lagging, soda ash up about 10%, no raw-material pass-through, and a 75-day SG1/SG2 rebuild likely in H1 FY28 that management will not guarantee volume recovery from.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Rooftop solar launched in four states at early stage with distributors appointed, but no product timeline or revenue target was quantified.

rows.label: Dolomite sourcing shift to domestic supply
rows.why: Dolomite sourcing is 30-40% domestic and management plans to shift toward more domestic supply to offset soda ash (30-32% of raw material cost) and freight inflation, but no savings were quantified.

rows.label: Net cash positive by end-March 2027
rows.why: Management expects to be net cash positive by end-March 2027 while funding the INR1,100 crore project internally with INR300 crore sanctioned debt undrawn.

rows.label: Overseas subsidiaries loss narrowing
rows.why: Overseas EBITDA improved to negative INR0.11 crore in Q2 FY27 from negative INR5.08 crore a year earlier, with nil revenue.

tone.note: Management was confident on the October output rebound, the 600 tpd line timing and the 31-32% margin path, but cautious on volume make-up (called speculative), the SG1/SG2 rebuild and tax and cash-flow queries (deferred to IR); analysts pushed on margins, raw-material costs and funding.
